name: Kybern UI Login
author: KybernAI

sections.description:
Kybern UI Login gives administrators a focused way to brand the native WordPress login screen without editing a theme or maintaining PHP snippets.

Choose a logo from the WordPress Media Library and the settings screen analyses its dominant colours and their approximate positions directly in your browser. Those values create a subtle, light gradient background while accessible action colours keep buttons, links, and focus states readable.

Getting started

After installing and activating Kybern UI Login, sign in as an administrator and select Appearance > Kybern UI Login in the left-hand WordPress admin menu. Choose your logo, adjust the colours, and preview your login page before saving.

You can also open Appearance > Themes, click your active theme to view its details, and select Kybern UI Login where that button is available. Both routes open the same login branding settings.

Features:

  • Select, replace, or remove a dedicated login logo through the Media Library.
  • Fall back automatically to the active theme’s custom logo.
  • Link the logo to the website home page and use the site name as accessible link text.
  • Analyse two distinct logo colours and their positions without server image libraries.
  • Fine-tune colours and gradient positions manually.
  • Preview changes before saving.
  • Reset branding to safe defaults.
  • Keep lost-password, registration, privacy, language, 2FA, and security-plugin states usable.
  • Load CSS only on WordPress login screens and plugin assets only on its settings page.

The plugin uses no remote APIs, tracking, third-party libraries, front-end assets, or custom database tables. It stores one versioned option containing the selected attachment ID and final colour settings. Image pixels never leave the browser and are never saved.

Privacy

Kybern UI Login does not collect, transmit, or track personal data. Logo analysis happens locally in the administrator’s browser and no image-pixel data is stored. When a selected Media Library image is served from remote storage, an administrator-requested analysis may retrieve that image through WordPress so the browser can examine it. The plugin does not send site or user data to analytics services or other third parties.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the kybern-ui-login folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Kybern UI Login.
  3. In the left-hand admin menu, open Appearance > Kybern UI Login. Alternatively, open Appearance > Themes, view your active theme’s details, and click Kybern UI Login where available.
  4. Select a Media Library logo or use the active theme custom logo.
  5. Review the automatic colour analysis and live preview, then save.
  6. Open the normal WordPress login page in a private browser window to confirm the result.
sections.faq:
What happens if I do not select a plugin logo?

The plugin uses the active theme’s WordPress custom logo. If no custom logo exists, WordPress keeps its standard login logo.

Which image formats can I use?

PNG, JPEG, and WebP images work when WordPress accepts them. SVG images work only when the site already permits SVG uploads.

Does automatic colour analysis upload my logo anywhere?

No. Analysis runs in the settings-page browser with an off-screen canvas. Only the final colours and positions are saved.

Can I adjust the generated design?

Yes. Both colours and their horizontal and vertical positions can be adjusted before saving. Manual mode prevents future logo selections from running automatically.

Will this affect the public website?

No. Login styles load only on WordPress login screens. Settings assets load only under Appearance > Kybern UI Login.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivation immediately restores the normal WordPress login presentation and keeps your settings. Deleting the plugin removes only its own settings option.
